item.title: Breaking the Debt Trap: Why Spending Smarter Beats Spending More
item.description: In this commentary, Philip Luck and Michael H. Gary argue efficient public spending is the key to unlocking growth in challenging fiscal environments characterized by rising debt and slowing growth.

item.title: Progress at the Much-Delayed New Yalu River Bridge
item.description: Satellite imagery shows that North Korea has made significant progress at the port-of-entry site for the much-delayed New Yalu River Bridge.

item.title: Navigating the Divide: Why the U.S. Navy Must Resume FONOPs in Indonesia
item.description: For nearly a decade, the U.S. has quietly acquiesced to Indonesia’s restrictive maritime claims to avoid diplomatic friction. This policy has failed. To prevent a catastrophic loss of access during a future crisis, the U.S. Navy must resume targeted Freedom of Navigation Operations.

item.title: Experts React: The NSS and Washington’s New Approach to the Western Hemisphere
item.description: CSIS Americas experts weigh in on the implications of the U.S. National Security Strategy for the Western Hemisphere.

item.title: From Production to Procurement: How Europe and Ukraine are Transforming Defense Supply Chains
item.description: To sustain Ukraine’s wartime industrial surge, partners must keep channeling allied funds directly into Ukrainian production. The Danish model transforms support by unlocking capacity, expanding purchasing power, and embedding unprecedented transparency in procurement.

item.title: Framing a U.S. Approach to the West Bank
item.description: Issues of the West Bank's current status are uniquely difficult because they combine ancient historical claims, modern nationalism, differing religious worldviews, and contemporary security dilemmas.

item.title: Creeping Sovereignty? China’s Maritime Structures in the Yellow Sea (West Sea)
item.description: China's placement of structures in and around the Yellow Sea and harassment of South Korean vessels resemble “creeping sovereignty” grey zone tactics that Beijing employed in the militarization of the South and East China Seas. What should the U.S. and Korea do to respond?

item.title: The Drone Supply Chain War: Identifying the Chokepoints to Making a Drone
item.description: China controls the critical materials that underpin modern drone warfare. The U.S. defense industrial base is dangerously dependent. This article reveals the five strategic chokepoints and four steps for building industrial resilience to secure future combat power.
